items.prose: Detailed 1:25,000 contour survey of the central detonation crater. The basin floor is paved with a continuous three-inch pavement of translucent olive-green trinitite glass; gamma dosimeters register 18.5 R/hr at ground level, dropping to 4.2 R/hr along the outer ejecta rim.

Topographic map illustrating prevailing southwesterly fallout plumes across the crest. The windward granite face is encrusted with dense black fallout dust (6.8 R/hr), while the leeward cliff face lies in a deep radiation shadow with readings below 0.1 R/hr.

Mapping of the four-meter-deep silt deposits where mountain storm runoff empties into the valley floor. Fine particulate cobalt-60 and strontium-90 bound to river clay particles form an impassable delta of radioactive mud.

Topographic sink with 200-meter sheer rim walls. Atmospheric temperature inversions trap heavy radon-222 gas and stagnant sulfur dioxide fog in the caldera floor; traversing the bottom without positive-pressure air supply causes acute suffocation.

A thirty-meter-deep blasting cut through solid basalt bedrock excavated for the pre-war railway. The steep stone walls provide 85% geometric gamma attenuation from surface fallout, creating the safest north-south scavenger transit corridor in the region.

Forty square kilometers of dead, brick-red pine timber killed by initial prompt radiation. The wood does not decompose due to the absence of soil fungi and insects; a massive dry fuel load that presents an extreme risk of catastrophic radioactive forest fires.

A narrow, sinuous gravel ridge rising fifteen meters above the surrounding flooded muskeg. The fast-draining coarse sand and lack of fine silt prevent radioactive particle accumulation, offering excellent visibility and firm footing for laden sledges.

Contour overlay of the earthen dam breach at Uranium Mine 9. Five million tons of acidic radium-bearing slime swept three miles down the creek bed, burying highway bridges under two meters of toxic grey mud that emits 14 R/hr.
